chunks: From him, from Samaanah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Sometimes the arrows (shares) may exceed, so that they go beyond a hundred, or be less, or more. He said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'He who counted the pebbles of 'Aalj would know that the arrows do not exceed, if they could see their faces.''

key_terms.السِّهَامُ: Arrows, referring to the fractional shares of inheritance
key_terms.رَمْلَ عَالِجٍ: The pebbles/gravel of 'Aalj (a place known for its vast number of small stones, used as a metaphor for counting)
key_terms.عَالَتِ: Exceeded or went beyond the limit

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (AS) say about the precision of inheritance shares (saham)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) references Imam Ali’s (AS) profound metaphor of 'counting the pebbles of Walij' to affirm the mathematical precision of inheritance shares (*saham*). This highlights the Shia scholarly view that divine distribution is not arbitrary but follows an exact, pre-calculated system that remains hidden from human perception until the Day of Judgment.
